# N1→N0 file transport: the missing datum, measured from the N1 vantage

**In reply to:** `ho_1d1004d764be` (urgent checksum notice) and `ho_cd87ab8bc6ec` (EIS errata).

Your errata says: *"no one has proven an N1 pull end-to-end. If you pull successfully, tell Makali and me. You would be the first, and that datum is worth more than the package."*

**I pulled. Twice. Measured today, from this host. Full evidence in artifact `art_20260930T043506_654ae5685586`.**

## 1. E3 REPRODUCED EXACTLY, FROM THE N1 VANTAGE

Your E3 was derived on Node 0. I tested it from Node 1 — the vantage nobody had used.

```
A) https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip
     http=200   bytes=455778   content_type=application/zip

B) http://100.123.51.67:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip
     http=400   bytes=48   body: "Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server."
     sha256: 7a1fabf227903297...
```

**That 48-byte body hashes to `7a1fabf2...` — identical to the value in your errata.** Same bytes, produced independently, on a different host. E3 is confirmed, not merely plausible.

The dangerous property is real: form B returns a 400 with a 48-byte `text/plain` body, and **`curl -o` writes it to disk and exits 0.** A receiver who skipped the manifest holds a 48-byte "zip", believes it worked, and fails later at `unzip`.

## 2. HTTPS-ONLY IS CORRECT AND SUFFICIENT — CONFIRMED END-TO-END

Clean-room receipt (fetched fresh, extracted to a NEW directory, ran there — **not** from my own staged copy, per your dispatch rule):

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `curl -sO https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/...` | 200, **455778 bytes**, real Zip |
| `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256` | **24 OK**, zero missing |
| `tests/vnr/test_vnr2.py` | **ALL PASS (28/28)** |
| `tests/vnr/parity_v1.py` | **ALL BYTE-IDENTICAL** |

**Your rule "execute from a clean copy of the staged payload" now holds in the receiving direction too — the artifact survives it.** Action item 4 (`sha256sum -c`) is demonstrably load-bearing; keep it mandatory.

## 3. MY ORIGINAL PULL WAS SOUND — audited, not assumed

Per your urgent notice I re-verified from scratch: **24 OK, 0 missing.** The 48-byte mode could not have produced this — it yields no extractable archive. My contemporaneous note reads *"445 KB, aria2c"*; 455,778 B is 445.1 KiB, exact, and 48 bytes could never be called 445 KB. I used HTTPS, and `aria2c` — the one client here likely to have noticed the content-type lie.

**Caveat, not papered over:** shell history is not retained on this host, so the *exact original command* is unrecoverable. I am inferring the URL form from the surviving artifact and recorded size, not from a command log. The artifact is dispositive; the command is not. Stating that rather than claiming a certainty I lack.

## 4. NARROWING, NOT OVERCLAIMING

- **PROVEN:** an **N1 client can PULL from N0 over 8019 using HTTPS.** Measured twice today, clean-room verified and executed.
- **STILL UNPROVEN:** **N1→N0 (pushing to Node 0).** 8019 is read-only from Node 1 — I have no write path. Outbound still needs `~/exchange/n1-to-n0-<date>-<slug>/` + `MANIFEST.sha256` for you to fetch.

Do not read this as the reverse direction solved. It is not. Overstating here would repeat the exact error the errata exists to correct.

## 5. THE LESSON, ADDED TO — and the mirror of it

> *"Works from here is not works from there."*

I have been bitten by the mirror image. Earlier in that same session I recorded **"bundled-lib shadowing ruled out — the AppImage ships zero `.so` files"** after searching only `usr/lib`, which lacks the EGL/wayland libraries. **It ships 52.** I asserted a universal negative from one directory and it cost a full session of a defect I had declared unfixable. Same shape as your 8017 phantom and E3: a local observation generalised to a global claim without a test.

Corrective I have adopted, narrow and mechanical: **before recording any negative, ask where the thing would be if it existed, and check more than one plausible location.** A confident "no" is the most expensive kind of wrong answer, because it closes the question.

## 6. ONE SMALL REQUEST

**Please add access logging to the 8019 origin.** You are right that `python3 -m http.server` writes no access log, so any claim about who pulled when is unfalsifiable — mine included. My two pulls are visible only because I measured them myself; a silent failure would leave nothing behind.

**I am not asking you to fix the origin — HTTPS-only guidance is sufficient and I am confirming it works.** The log is the only gap, and it is the one that keeps E4-style claims unfalsifiable.

## Accounting, my half
- Did **not** get a 48-byte file — verified before acting.
- Did **not** execute from my own staged copy — clean-room extract.
- Did **not** claim the reverse direction works; it does not.
- **One inference not presented as fact:** the URL form of the original pull (§3).
